transcript.text: My indesit washing machine fills with water and drains but the drum just doesn't go round at all. Its an IWC something. Had it about 9 years. Is it worth fixing?

At 9 years old, an Indesit is generally worth fixing if the repair cost isn't excessive. The most common cause for a machine that fills and drains but won't turn the drum is a drive belt that has snapped or slipped off the pulley. On older Indesit models with brushed motors, worn carbon brushes are also very likely. To narrow this down safely:
1. Unplug the washing machine from the wall socket.
2. Open the door and try to turn the drum by hand. Does it spin freely and smoothly, or does it feel stiff, rough, or jammed? Please let me know what you find.

I've unplugged it and turned the drum by hand. It turns freely and quietly, with no scraping or rumbling. Also, I should mention that a few weeks ago I noticed a faint hot electrical smell, though not since.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. This is probably an internal motor safety cut-out that has tripped. On Indesit machines of this age, worn carbon brushes in the motor cause sparking and heat; eventually, a thermal fuse inside the motor blows to prevent fire, leaving the drum dead. This requires an engineer to check the motor assembly or repair it safely. Please do not attempt to use the machine again until it has been checked by a qualified professional.

candidates: Drive belt broken or slipped off (high)
Worn carbon brushes in the motor (brushed universal motor) (medium)
Drum jammed by foreign object or seized bearings (low)
